source: clementina-rom/src/basic/token.s, program.s, misc1.s, inline.s, defines_clementina.s, and the statement and function handlers in the stock and clementina_*.s sources

runtimeDebug.source: current ROM kernel.lbl symbols NEWSTT2=$1E91, CURLIN=$0041 and VARTAB=$0035 (ARYTAB follows at $0037)
runtimeDebug.behavior: NEWSTT2 runs immediately before each statement dispatch, after CURLIN is updated for a new numbered line; an address breakpoint there can be filtered by the little-endian CURLIN value

savedProgram.contents: raw TXTTAB..VARTAB bytes; no PRG header
savedProgram.loadBehavior: LOAD rebuilds every forward link before entering READY

styleSidecar.literalOffsetBase: first tokenized-text byte after the four-byte line header
styleSidecar.plainSourceCompiler: does not emit sidecars because text source has no per-cell attributes

lexicalBehavior.spaces: leading spaces after the line number are skipped; subsequent spaces are preserved
lexicalBehavior.case: ASCII uppercase outside quoted strings, DATA, and REM
lexicalBehavior.hexNumber: a $ not right after a letter or digit is followed by its hex digits as typed (uppercased), so CD and DEF inside a hex number are not keywords

notes: One entry per ROM token, in token-table order: primary, MON, extension, extension2, then extension functions.
kind is statement, function, operator, or keyword (a word that only appears inside another statement, such as TO).
syntax uses [ ] for optional parts, ... for repeats, and | between alternative forms; argument names appear in it in order.
An argument outside min..max raises ILLEGAL QUANTITY unless its note names another error. Without min and max BASIC checks no range.
Where min and max are given, the value is rounded down to a whole number before the check.
A string where a number is expected, or the reverse, raises TYPE MISMATCH.

A number can be written in hex as $ and 1 to 6 hex digits (0-16777215); a digit past $FFFFFF raises OVERFLOW. The tokenizer keeps the digits after a $ as typed, so $CD00 never holds the CD keyword, unless the $ follows a letter or digit and so ends a string variable name (A$).

argumentTypes.path: String expression naming an SD card file or directory, relative to the current directory (CD) or absolute from /. An SD error raises FILE I/O ERROR.
argumentTypes.handle: File number 1-16 of a file opened with OPEN.
argumentTypes.line-number: Line number written as literal digits, not an expression. For GOTO, GOSUB, THEN, ON and RUN a line that does not exist raises UNDEF'D STATEMENT; LIST lists nothing for it.
argumentTypes.condition: Numeric expression where 0 is false and any other value is true.
argumentTypes.variable: Numeric or string variable, or array element, that receives a value.
argumentTypes.numeric-variable: Numeric variable, or array element, that receives a value.
argumentTypes.name: Name of a DEF FN function, written like a numeric variable name right after FN.
argumentTypes.statement: One or more statements separated by colons.
argumentTypes.text: Characters stored as typed, up to the end of the statement or line.
argumentTypes.keyword: One of a fixed set of words, listed in the note.

entries.summary: Ends the program, stops background music and returns to the READY prompt.

arguments.name: variable
arguments.note: Simple numeric variable; an integer (%) variable or array element gives SYNTAX ERROR. A FOR on a variable already looping replaces that loop.

arguments.name: start
arguments.note: Assigned to the variable when the loop starts.

arguments.name: end
arguments.note: Evaluated once. The test is made at NEXT, so the body runs at least once.

arguments.name: step
arguments.note: Defaults to 1; a negative step counts down and STEP 0 never ends.

entries.summary: Starts a loop: sets the variable to start and repeats the body up to NEXT, adding step (default 1) until it passes end; the body runs at least once.

arguments.name: variable
arguments.note: Omitted: the innermost loop. Naming an outer loop closes the inner ones; with no matching FOR, NEXT WITHOUT FOR.

entries.summary: Ends a FOR loop: adds the step and loops back while the limit is not passed; NEXT I,J closes several loops in turn.

arguments.name: value
arguments.note: Number or string constant. Quoted strings may hold commas and colons; unquoted ones end at a comma or colon.

entries.summary: Holds constants that READ takes in program order; executing a DATA statement does nothing.

arguments.name: prompt
arguments.note: A quoted string literal followed by a semicolon; "? " is printed after it.

arguments.name: variable
arguments.note: Missing items prompt ??, a bad number asks to REDO FROM START and extra items print EXTRA IGNORED.

entries.summary: Reads values typed in the screen editor into variables; program mode only, and an empty line stops the run (CONT resumes).

arguments.name: array
arguments.note: Float, integer (%) or string array name.

arguments.name: dimensions
arguments.note: Highest subscript of each dimension, separated by commas; a dimension holds one more element than its highest subscript.

entries.summary: Creates arrays with the given highest subscripts, starting at 0; an array used without DIM gets 0-10 per dimension, and a second DIM gives REDIM'D ARRAY.

arguments.name: variable
arguments.note: A non-numeric item read into a numeric variable gives SYNTAX ERROR on the DATA line; reading past the last item gives OUT OF DATA.

entries.summary: Assigns the next DATA items, in program order, to the listed variables.

arguments.name: variable
arguments.note: An integer (%) variable takes the floored value and must be -32768 to 32767. TI accepts 0-5183999.

entries.summary: Assigns an expression to a variable; the word LET is optional. Assigning TI sets the 60 Hz clock.
Jumps to the given line number.

arguments.name: line
arguments.note: Omitted: the first line.

entries.summary: Clears variables, arrays, strings, the DATA pointer and the FOR/GOSUB stack, then runs the program from its start or from the given line.

entries.syntax: IF condition THEN line|statement | IF condition GOTO line

arguments.name: condition
arguments.note: 0 is false and any other number true; comparisons give -1 or 0. Strings cannot be tested.

arguments.name: line
arguments.note: After THEN or GOTO, the line to jump to when the condition is true.

arguments.name: statement
arguments.note: After THEN, the rest of the line, run only when the condition is true. There is no ELSE.

entries.summary: Tests a condition: when true it jumps to a line or runs the rest of the line, otherwise it continues with the next line.
Resets the DATA pointer so the next READ starts at the first DATA item; it takes no line number (RESTORE 10 is a SYNTAX ERROR).
Calls the subroutine at the given line; RETURN resumes after the GOSUB. Nesting too deep gives OUT OF MEMORY.
Returns from the most recent GOSUB, dropping any FOR loops opened inside it; with no GOSUB active it gives RETURN WITHOUT GOSUB.

arguments.name: text
arguments.note: Stored as typed, not tokenized.

entries.summary: Marks the rest of the line as a comment; nothing after REM on that line runs.
Stops the program with BREAK IN line and stops background music; CONT resumes after it. Ctrl-C between statements does the same.

arguments.name: index
arguments.note: Truncated; 0 or a value past the end of the list continues with the next statement.

entries.summary: Jumps to (GOTO) or calls (GOSUB) the line at position index in the list; 0 or a position past the end continues.

arguments.name: address
arguments.note: CPU address.

arguments.name: invert
arguments.note: Defaults to 0; its set bits are inverted before masking.

entries.summary: Pauses until (PEEK(address) XOR invert) AND mask is nonzero; the loop does not check Ctrl-C, so a condition that never comes true hangs the machine.

arguments.name: path
arguments.note: A failed open leaves the current program in memory; a program too large for BASIC memory gives FILE I/O ERROR.

entries.summary: Replaces the program with a tokenized BASIC file from the SD card, clears variables and ends at READY, even when a program runs it.
Writes the current program's tokenized text (TXTTAB to VARTAB, no header) to a file on the SD card, creating or truncating it.

arguments.name: name
arguments.note: Numeric function name written right after FN, as in FNA; a string name gives TYPE MISMATCH.

arguments.name: variable
arguments.note: The one simple numeric parameter.

arguments.name: expression
arguments.note: The function body; it is not evaluated until FN is called.

entries.summary: Defines a one-argument numeric function FNname for later use in expressions; program mode only (ILLEGAL DIRECT in direct mode).

arguments.name: address
arguments.note: CPU address; $8000-$BFFF writes the bank BANK picked (bank 0 is mapped again afterwards), and $C000 and up reach I/O and the MIA registers.

entries.summary: Writes a byte to a CPU memory address.

arguments.name: bank
arguments.note: Palette bank of the BASIC pen; its flip and ALT bits are kept.

entries.summary: Sets the BASIC pen palette (0-15) used for READY, error messages, INPUT prompts, numbers and unstyled text; the editor pen is not changed.

arguments.name: enabled
arguments.note: 0 off, any other value on.

entries.summary: Turns the horizontal flip on (nonzero) or off (0) in the BASIC pen used for messages and unstyled output.

arguments.name: enabled
arguments.note: 0 off, any other value on.

entries.summary: Turns the vertical flip on (nonzero) or off (0) in the BASIC pen used for messages and unstyled output.

arguments.name: enabled
arguments.note: 0 off, any other value on.

entries.summary: Turns the alternate (reverse) character bank on (nonzero) or off (0) in the BASIC pen used for messages and unstyled output.

arguments.name: mask
arguments.note: Bit 0 color, bit 1 flip X, bit 2 flip Y, bit 3 ALT. A set bit makes styled strings take that field from the BASIC pen; 0 keeps their own.

entries.summary: Chooses which attribute fields (1 color, 2 flip-X, 4 flip-Y, 8 ALT) printed styled strings take from the BASIC pen instead of their own.
Moves the text cursor to column 0-39, row 0-24 (0,0 is the top-left corner) and sets BASIC's column counter to match.
Clears the screen, homes the cursor and resets BASIC's column counter to 0.

arguments.name: expression
arguments.note: A comma moves to the next 14-column zone and a semicolon adds no space; a trailing comma or semicolon keeps the cursor on the line. ? is short for PRINT.

entries.summary: Prints values; strings keep their stored per-character colors and attributes, while numbers and unstyled text use the BASIC pen set by COLOR.
Continues a program stopped by STOP, Ctrl-C or an empty INPUT line; after an error, a program edit, NEW, CLEAR, RUN or LOAD it gives CAN'T CONTINUE.

arguments.name: start
arguments.note: LIST n lists only line n.

arguments.name: end
arguments.note: LIST n- lists to the end and LIST -m from the first line.

entries.summary: Lists program lines, all or a range, with string literals in their stored colors, then returns to READY (a LIST inside a program ends the run).
Clears all variables, arrays and strings and resets the DATA pointer and FOR/GOSUB stack; Clementina spells it CLEAR (not CLR) and it takes no argument.

arguments.name: variable
arguments.note: A string variable gets the key; a numeric variable accepts only a digit key, and any other key gives SYNTAX ERROR.

entries.summary: Waits for a key for each variable and stores it without echo; program mode only (ILLEGAL DIRECT in direct mode).
Erases the program and all variables and stops background music; inside a running program it also ends the run.

arguments.name: column
arguments.note: Nothing is printed when output is already at or past that column.

entries.summary: Inside PRINT, prints spaces up to the given column; it is not valid elsewhere and returns no value.

entries.syntax: FOR variable=start TO end | GO TO line
entries.summary: Separates the start value from the limit in FOR, and follows GO in GO TO; it is not a statement by itself.

arguments.name: argument
arguments.note: The parameter variable's own value is restored after the call.

returns.note: Value of the DEF FN body.

entries.summary: Calls a function defined with DEF FNname, passing one numeric argument; an undefined name gives UNDEF'D FUNCTION.
Inside PRINT, prints the given number of spaces (0-255); it is not valid elsewhere and returns no value.
Follows the condition in IF; GOTO may stand in its place when jumping to a line.

arguments.name: value
arguments.note: Floored to an integer first. NOT binds looser than comparisons, so NOT A=B is NOT (A=B).

entries.summary: Bitwise NOT of a 16-bit integer, giving -value-1, so NOT 0 is -1 (true) and NOT -1 is 0 (false).

entries.syntax: FOR variable=start TO end STEP step
entries.summary: Sets the amount added to the FOR variable on each NEXT (default 1); a negative step counts down.

arguments.name: left
arguments.note: Omitted for unary plus, which does nothing.

returns.note: The sum of two numbers, or two strings joined (at most 255 characters, else STRING TOO LONG).

arguments.note: Omitted for negation.

returns.note: OVERFLOW beyond about 1.70141183E+38.

arguments.note: 0 gives DIVISION BY ZERO.

arguments.note: A negative base needs a whole exponent, else ILLEGAL QUANTITY.

entries.summary: Raises a number to a power, with the highest precedence; a negative base needs an integer exponent, otherwise ILLEGAL QUANTITY.

arguments.name: left
arguments.note: Floored to an integer first.

arguments.note: Floored to an integer first.

arguments.note: Floored to an integer first.

arguments.name: right
arguments.note: Floored to an integer first.

arguments.note: Same type as left, else TYPE MISMATCH.

returns.note: -1 when true, 0 when false. Strings compare by character code; >= and <> combine the signs.

entries.summary: Greater-than comparison of two numbers or two strings (by character code), giving -1 if true and 0 if false.

arguments.name: right
arguments.note: Same type as left, else TYPE MISMATCH.

returns.note: -1 when true, 0 when false. Strings compare by character code. The same token is the assignment sign in LET, FOR and DEF.

entries.summary: Equality comparison of two numbers or two strings (by character code), giving -1 if true and 0 if false.

arguments.name: right
arguments.note: Same type as left, else TYPE MISMATCH.

returns.note: -1 when true, 0 when false. Strings compare by character code; <= and <> combine the signs.

entries.summary: Less-than comparison of two numbers or two strings (by character code), giving -1 if true and 0 if false.
Returns -1, 0 or 1 for a negative, zero or positive number.

returns.note: Values of 2^31 or more are returned unchanged.

entries.summary: Returns the largest integer not greater than the number (floor), so INT(-1.5) is -2.
Returns the absolute value of a number.

arguments.name: value
arguments.note: Passed in the floating-point accumulator; any type.

returns.note: The number the routine leaves in the accumulator; the default vector gives ILLEGAL QUANTITY.

entries.summary: Calls the machine-code routine named by the USR vector in zero page, passing the argument in the floating-point accumulator.

arguments.name: value
arguments.note: Ignored.

returns.note: Signed 16-bit, so more than 32767 free bytes would read negative.

entries.summary: Collects unused strings and returns the free bytes between the arrays and the string heap; the argument is ignored.

arguments.name: value
arguments.note: Ignored.

returns.note: BASIC's output column counter, set to 0 by a new line, CLS or CRSR.

entries.summary: Returns BASIC's output column counter (0-255); the argument is ignored.
Returns the square root, computed as X^0.5; a negative argument gives ILLEGAL QUANTITY.

arguments.name: number
arguments.note: Positive: next number. 0: repeats the last number. Negative: reseeds from the argument (the same value restarts the same sequence).

returns.note: Less than 1. The sequence is the same after every cold start unless reseeded.

entries.summary: Returns a pseudo-random number from 0 up to 1: a positive argument gives the next one, 0 repeats the last, a negative one reseeds.

arguments.name: number
arguments.note: Must be greater than 0; 0 or negative gives ILLEGAL QUANTITY.

entries.summary: Returns the natural logarithm; the argument must be greater than 0, else ILLEGAL QUANTITY.

arguments.name: number
arguments.note: Above about 88.03 the result exceeds the float range and gives OVERFLOW; very negative values give 0.

entries.summary: Returns e raised to the number; results beyond the float range (argument above about 88.03) give OVERFLOW.

arguments.name: number
arguments.note: Radians.

entries.summary: Returns the cosine of an angle in radians.

arguments.name: number
arguments.note: Radians.

entries.summary: Returns the sine of an angle in radians.

arguments.name: number
arguments.note: Radians.

returns.note: Computed as SIN/COS; DIVISION BY ZERO only if the computed cosine is exactly 0.

entries.summary: Returns the tangent of an angle in radians.

returns.note: Radians, between -PI/2 and PI/2.

entries.summary: Returns the arctangent, in radians, between -PI/2 and PI/2.

arguments.name: address
arguments.note: CPU address; $8000-$BFFF reads the bank BANK picked (bank 0 is mapped again afterwards).

entries.summary: Returns the byte (0-255) at a CPU memory address.

returns.note: Characters only; attribute bytes are not counted.

entries.summary: Returns the number of characters in a string (0-255).

returns.note: Up to 9 significant digits, with E notation for large or small values.

entries.summary: Converts a number to the text PRINT would show, with a leading space for positive numbers or a minus sign.
Converts the leading decimal number in a string to its value, or 0 if there is none; hex $ prefixes are not recognized.

arguments.name: string
arguments.note: An empty string gives ILLEGAL QUANTITY.

entries.summary: Returns the code (0-255) of the first character of a string; an empty string gives ILLEGAL QUANTITY.

returns.note: One character, with the default attribute ($00).

entries.summary: Returns a one-character string with the given code (0-255).

arguments.name: length
arguments.note: 0 gives an empty string; a length past the end returns the whole string.

returns.note: Keeps the characters' attributes.

entries.summary: Returns the leftmost length characters of a string (all of it if shorter), keeping their attributes.

arguments.name: length
arguments.note: 0 gives an empty string; a length past the end returns the whole string.

returns.note: Keeps the characters' attributes.

entries.summary: Returns the rightmost length characters of a string (all of it if shorter), keeping their attributes.

arguments.name: start
arguments.note: 1-based; past the end gives an empty string.

arguments.name: length
arguments.note: Omitted: the rest of the string.

returns.note: Keeps the characters' attributes.

entries.summary: Returns length characters of a string starting at position start (1-based), or the rest of the string when length is omitted.
Two-word form of GOTO, written GO TO line; GO SUB is not supported.
Enters the WozMon machine-code monitor; typing Q there returns to BASIC's READY prompt with the program and variables kept.

arguments.name: bank
arguments.note: Palette bank whose ink color becomes the screen backdrop; 6 restores the default blue.

entries.summary: Sets the screen backdrop to the ink color of a palette bank, the same color COLOR gives text.
Starts the MIA sound generator (audio starts stopped); set voices up first, then SNDON once.
Stops the sound generator; voice registers are kept.
Stops the sound generator, clears every voice and restores the audio defaults.

arguments.name: voice
arguments.note: Given, the statement sets that voice's volume trim instead of the master volume.

arguments.name: level
arguments.note: Master volume 0-15 (0 mutes, 16 and up give ILLEGAL QUANTITY), or a voice trim 0-255 where 255 is unity.

entries.summary: Sets the master volume (0-15), or with a voice number sets that voice's volume trim (0-255, 255 = unity).

arguments.name: waveform
arguments.note: 0 sine, 1 pulse, 2 saw, 3 triangle, 4 noise.

entries.summary: Selects a voice's waveform: 0 sine, 1 pulse, 2 saw, 3 triangle or 4 noise.

arguments.name: note
arguments.note: Semitone: octave*12 + step, so 48 is middle C (C4) and 57 is A4 at 440 Hz. The envelope restarts from its attack.

entries.summary: Plays a semitone (0-95) on a voice, starting a new note with its envelope and waveform restarted.

arguments.name: hz
arguments.note: Whole hertz; the pitch changes without a new attack.

entries.summary: Sets a voice's pitch in whole hertz (0-4095) without restarting the note.

arguments.name: enabled
arguments.note: 0 releases the note; any other value gates it on without retriggering.

entries.summary: Gates a voice's note on without retriggering (non-zero) or releases it so it fades out (0).

arguments.name: attack
arguments.note: Attack rate; lower is faster.

arguments.name: decay
arguments.note: Decay rate; lower is faster.

arguments.name: sustain
arguments.note: Sustain level, not a rate: 0 silent, 15 full.

arguments.name: release
arguments.note: Release rate; lower is faster.

entries.summary: Sets a voice's envelope: attack, decay and release rates and the sustain level, each 0-15.

arguments.name: width
arguments.note: Duty cycle, 128 being about square; only the pulse waveform uses it.

entries.summary: Sets a voice's pulse duty cycle (0-255, 128 about square); only affects the pulse waveform.

arguments.name: position
arguments.note: -64 hard left, 0 centre, 63 hard right.

entries.summary: Sets a voice's stereo position from -64 (hard left) through 0 (centre) to 63 (hard right).
Turns the background (playfield) layer on.
Turns the background (playfield) layer off.

arguments.name: mode
arguments.note: Virtual map size in cells: 0 = 40x25 (no scroll headroom), 1 = 80x25, 2 = 40x50, 3 = 160x25, 4 = 40x100, 5 = 80x50. The display stays 320x200.

entries.summary: Selects how the background's raw 40x25 tables tile into one scrollable map (modes 0-5).

arguments.name: set
arguments.note: 0 draws from tables 0-3, 1 from tables 4-7.

entries.summary: Selects which of the two background table sets (0 or 1) the current BGMODE arrangement is drawn from.

arguments.name: x
arguments.note: Pixels; wraps at the width of the current BGMODE map.

arguments.name: y
arguments.note: Pixels; wraps at the height of the current BGMODE map.

entries.summary: Pans the 320x200 view across the background map by x,y pixels, wrapping at the map's edges.
Selects the CHR bank (0-7) the background layer normally draws its tiles from.
Selects the CHR bank (0-7) used for background cells whose attribute has the CHR_ALT bit set.
Turns the whole sprite layer on.
Turns the whole sprite layer off.
Sets the highest sprite (OAM) index, 0-255, that the renderer scans each frame.
Selects the CHR bank (0-7) that sprites draw their tiles from.

arguments.name: is1bpp

arguments.name: background
arguments.note: Plane of a 1bpp bank the background decodes.

arguments.note: Plane of a 1bpp bank sprites decode.

arguments.note: Plane of a 1bpp bank the overlay (text) layer decodes.

arguments.name: index
arguments.note: Color within the bank.

arguments.note: 5-bit red.

arguments.name: tile
arguments.note: Nametable tile code.

notes: An error prints a new line, then ?, the message and ERROR, then IN and the line number when a program is running, and returns to READY. The whole line uses the BASIC pen.
An error stops background music, clears the FOR/GOSUB stack and makes CONT impossible.
code is the error's byte offset in the ROM's ERROR_MESSAGES table, the value the interpreter's ERROR routine takes in X. The ROM build defines it as the entry's name.

Statements added for Clementina raise the standard errors: ILLEGAL QUANTITY for arguments outside the ranges in keywords.entries, TYPE MISMATCH, SYNTAX, OUT OF DATA for the DATA readers, and FILE I/O for SD errors.

entries.name: ERR_NOFOR
entries.trigger: NEXT ran with no FOR loop active, or named a variable that has no active loop.

entries.name: ERR_SYNTAX
entries.trigger: BASIC cannot parse the statement: an unknown or misspelled keyword, or a missing parenthesis, comma or quote. READ of a non-number into a numeric variable also raises it, on the DATA line.

entries.name: ERR_NOGOSUB
entries.trigger: RETURN ran with no GOSUB active.

entries.name: ERR_NODATA
entries.trigger: READ, or a statement that reads DATA (NTREAD, ATRREAD, CHRREAD, PALREAD, OAMREAD), ran past the last DATA item.

entries.name: ERR_ILLQTY
entries.trigger: A value is outside what a statement or function accepts: an argument outside a keyword's range, SQR of a negative number, LOG of 0 or less, or an integer (%) value outside -32768 to 32767.

entries.name: ERR_OVERFLOW
entries.trigger: A number is too large for BASIC (above about 1.7E38), or a hex number has a digit past $FFFFFF.

entries.name: ERR_MEMFULL
entries.trigger: The program, variables, arrays and strings no longer fit, or FOR loops, GOSUBs and parentheses nest too deeply for the stack.

entries.name: ERR_UNDEFSTAT
entries.trigger: GOTO, GOSUB, THEN, ON or RUN names a line number that does not exist.

entries.name: ERR_BADSUBS
entries.trigger: An array index is larger than the array's DIM (10 for an array used without DIM), or the number of indexes does not match.

entries.name: ERR_REDIMD
entries.trigger: DIM names an array that already exists, including one BASIC created when it was first used without DIM.

entries.name: ERR_ILLDIR
entries.trigger: INPUT, GET or DEF was typed as a direct command; they only work inside a program.

entries.name: ERR_BADTYPE
entries.trigger: A string where a number is expected or the reverse, such as comparing a string with a number or reading a file byte into a string variable.

entries.name: ERR_STRLONG
entries.trigger: A string result would be longer than 255 characters.

entries.name: ERR_FRMCPX
entries.trigger: A string expression needs more than three temporary strings at once, as with deeply nested string functions; split it with a variable.

entries.name: ERR_CANTCONT
entries.trigger: CONT has no stopped program to resume: nothing was stopped, or an error, a program edit, CLEAR, NEW or RUN came after the stop.

entries.name: ERR_UNDEFFN
entries.trigger: FN called a function that no DEF FN has defined.

entries.name: ERR_FILEIO
entries.trigger: An SD card or file operation failed: no card, a missing file or directory, a full card, a directory that is not empty, or a file number that is not open.

messages.name: ERREXTRA
messages.trigger: INPUT got more comma-separated values than it has variables. The extra values are dropped and the program continues.

messages.name: ERRREENTRY
messages.trigger: INPUT got text where it needs a number. It prints this and asks for the whole line again.

messages.name: QT_BREAK
messages.trigger: STOP ran, or Ctrl+C was pressed while a program ran. BASIC prints BREAK IN and the line number, and CONT resumes.
